The role

What an Admin can do

Admin is the control and coordination seat. You have full reach across the board and own the configuration that everyone else works inside.

You can

  • See and run every task — Overview, Board, List, Backlog
  • Create tasks and assign / reassign to any CS
  • Review QC, unlock overdue, reopen Done/Cancel
  • Clear the Unassigned queue
  • Manage Agent Groups, Categories and SLA Times

Check every day

  • Who is overloaded, who is free
  • Urgent / High and overdue tasks
  • Waiting or To Do stuck too long
  • Tasks with no assignee
  • Done tasks still waiting for QC

Shared
0202
QC Review · shared across roles

How QC closes the loop

Every task carries this panel once it's moved to Done or Cancel. Who reviews it differs by role; the panel itself doesn't.

Task detail · QC Review

Needs agent/admin QC lights up the moment a CS marks a task Done or Cancel.

  1. Reviewer opens the task, checks the work against the request.
  2. Marks QC checked if it's good — or Reopen with a reason if it isn't.
  3. The task stays visible as unreviewed until someone acts on it.

Admin & Agent — the reviewer

  • QC is a daily queue to clear, not a one-off check
  • Agent reviews their own team's CS; Admin can review anyone as a fallback
  • A reopen sends the task back with your reason attached — the CS sees exactly why

CS — the one being reviewed

  • Moving a task to Done or Cancel doesn't end it — QC still has to sign off
  • A Reopen notification means read the reason and pick the work back up
  • Clean, well-commented work moves through QC faster

Orientation

The Admin Task Board

Everything lives on one screen. Four views across the top, configuration on the right, filters and search below.

localhost:3000/tasks
  1. Four views — Overview, Board, List, Backlog. Switch freely; the filters carry across.
  2. Configuration — Agent Groups, Categories, SLA Times sit top-right.
  3. New task creates work; set assignee here or leave it for the queue.
  4. Filters + search narrow the board; the count on the right shows how many match.

Overview · 1 of 4

Read the workload at a glance

Overview is your decision screen. The top strip answers "how heavy is today?" before you touch a single task.

localhost:3000/tasks · Overview
  1. KPI strip — CS pool, open tasks, urgent/high load, needs-attention, unassigned.
  2. Attention areas — the biggest risks right now; click a bar to focus the CS table on those people.
  3. Work mix — open tasks by stage × priority, with overdue To Do / In Progress split out.

  4. SLA exposure is a workload proxy, not an ETA.

Overview · 2 of 4

CS workload table

One row per CS, sorted by pressure. This is where you decide who has room before assigning more.

localhost:3000/tasks · Overview
  1. Status — Overloaded Busy Free tells you capacity at a glance.
  2. Workload by stage — open / to do / in progress / waiting / overdue per person.
  3. SLA column — the tightest exposure and thresholds; a load signal, not a promise.
  4. Expand a row to inspect that person's actual tasks.

Overview · 3 of 4

Assign from the queue

Pick an unassigned task and the dashboard ranks who has room — then assign in one click, right here.

localhost:3000/tasks · Overview
  1. Choose a task in the Unassigned queue, or hit Recommend on any row.
  2. Assignment support ranks CS by projected load after adding this task.
  3. Each card shows open count, SLA exposure, in-progress and risk flags.

  4. Recommendation is support, not a replacement for your judgement.

Overview · 4 of 4

Exceptions & the full queue

Two safety nets at the bottom of Overview so nothing slips: work held by people outside the CS pool, and every task still waiting for an owner.

localhost:3000/tasks · Overview
  1. Assignments outside the CS pool — tasks held by non-CS accounts; expand to review and reassign.
  2. Unassigned queue — sort by priority, scan SLA, and Recommend straight into assignment.
  3. Clearing this queue every day is the single most useful admin habit.

Views

Board — run work by stage

Kanban columns for the task lifecycle. Drag cards between stages; the board enforces the workflow rules for you.

localhost:3000/tasks · Board
  1. Stages: To Do → In Progress → Waiting → Done → Cancel.
  2. An overdue card shows Enter reason — the unlock must be filled to keep working it.
  3. QC checked marks a reviewed Done; Reopen sends Done/Cancel back with a reason.

  4. Unassigned tasks stay in Backlog — they don't appear on the main board.

Views

List — audit many at once

A dense table for scanning and auditing. Sort any column, filter hard, and tick QC without leaving the row.

localhost:3000/tasks · List
  1. Columns: Key, Assignee, Summary, Category, Created, Priority, Status, QC.
  2. Filter by Agent / Assignee / Status / Priority / Overdue / Category; add a date range.
  3. Search runs across task text and comments.
  4. Click a row to open detail; tick QC if you have review rights.

Backlog — the unassigned pile

Every task without an owner waits here. Assign a CS and the task leaves Backlog and joins the live board.

localhost:3000/tasks · Backlog
  1. Pick the task to work; use the row's category / agent fields to triage.
  2. Assign a CS — the task moves straight into To Do on the board.
  3. Add a quick task inline at the bottom with the title / category / agent row.

New task

Capture the work on the left; set ownership on the right. Assign now, or leave it Unassigned to route through the queue.

localhost:3000/tasks · New task

Title → Description → Priority → Category → Agent → Assignee → Create.

Configuration

Agent Groups

Decides who owns and who can see what. Set the agents in the workflow, the CS on each agent's team, and who acts as an assistant.

localhost:3000/tasks · Agent Groups
  1. Selected agents on the left take part in the task workflow.
  2. CS members on the right are tied to the highlighted agent.
  3. Tick Assistant to let someone support an agent's scope.

  4. Update this whenever a CS joins, leaves, or switches team.

0213
Configuration

Categories

The task types CS pick from. They drive filtering, SLA rules, and workload-by-type reporting.

localhost:3000/tasks · Categories
  1. Each category carries a colour used on cards and pills.
  2. Add a new one with a name and colour; delete unused ones.

  3. Keep them clear — don't create categories that mean the same thing.

Admin
0214
Configuration

SLA Times

How long an In Progress task may run before it turns Overdue — set per priority, and overridable per category.

localhost:3000/tasks · SLA Times
  1. Pick a priority on the left (Low → Urgent).
  2. Set the default time, then override any category that needs its own.

  3. Review SLA when a category is added, or when Urgent/High throws too many false alarms.

Configuration

Reminder setup

Inside SLA Times, the Reminder Setup tab controls when the system nudges people about work that's slipping.

localhost:3000/tasks · SLA Times · Reminders
  1. Due soon — minutes before SLA ends to warn the assignee.
  2. To Do / Overdue / Waiting / Stale — hours before each reminder repeats.
  3. QC — hours a Done task can sit un-reviewed before a QC-stale nudge.

0218
Rhythm

The admin daily loop

A repeatable order of operations. Start wide on Overview, then drill into what's at risk.

1 · Open Overview

KPI strip and Attention areas first — where's the pressure today?

2 · Read Work mix

Stage × priority; note overdue To Do and In Progress.

3 · Scan CS table

Who's Overloaded, who's Free before assigning more.

4 · Clear Unassigned

Assign the queue using Recommend.

5 · Chase risk

Overdue, Waiting-stuck, To Do-stuck — follow up with CS/agent.

6 · Check QC

Review QC-stale Done tasks; reopen if not up to standard.

EPS · EXCEL PLANNING SOLUTIONS
Admin · remember

Overview first,
then act.

Recommendation supports your call — it never replaces it. Check workload, priority, overdue and waiting before you add more to anyone's plate. Keep the queue empty and QC current.
